questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, a destination I havn't visited before, university close to the city and nature, university with welcoming atmosphere and culture for exchange students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: KU and UNSW (University in Sydney) were helpful to provide information in the process of applying to the university, applying for visa etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived the day before orientation and received the information I needed study-wise at orientation day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The university in Sydney (UNSW) were sometimes pretty slow at replying to emails. To set up the student account and chose courses was time demanding (long waiting time for answers). So best tip is to be patient and know that they're also able to help you sort it all out when you are there in person.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a friend and knew where I was gonna live a couple of months before arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus was a great solution for me. I lived 25 min from campus by foot and got the opportunity to make friends at uni and outside of uni.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The first part was very straightforward. The university was good at sending emails and many reminders when there was another step to do.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
They send a lot of emails and the process was pretty easy to follow. Some of them ended up in spam which ended up causing me some trouble, however it worked out in the end. 
At first you apply to the host uni, get accepted and apply for visa.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to email and call the university. However, as the exchange got closer the university support also got more busy and answer time got pretty long.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Two of my initial chosen courses were full so I had to change. However, I ended up being happy about the courses I got.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of emails ending up in spam, and once registration for courses start and activation of student profile at the host institution be careful to it all before deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose two courses in my study and two courses outside my study. I would say that the level fitted me well, sometimes I felt that some of it was repetition of stuff I had already learned and other times it was knew approach (other methods, instruments in lab, computer programs). The two courses outside of my study were at a level so I could keep up, courses where it wasn't necessary with any prerequisites.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was a bit different and it was very obvious that the university had been shut down and doing online teaching during covid. Many of the Australian students hadn't been in lab in a while and in-person exercise classes were also just reestablished. The connection between students and with the professor was therefore a bit different from KU, where everybody knows each other and are used to work with one another in person.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Chemistry courses: Quantum Nature of Molecules, Environmental toxicology 
Others: Marine environment, Risks and Impacts of Changing Climate

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Environmental Toxicology was a good course and a course that is not offered in the BA at KU. 
Also intersting with the Risks and Impacts of Changing Climate

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Traveling around in the weekends and holidays will also be quite expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and eating out was expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of clubs, sports etc. offered and the social part of that seemed really cool. I joined the surf club and went surfing with them a couple of times. However, I lived in a house with a lot of international students and made friends in class, so my schedule was full doing activities with them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Exchange in Sydney calls for surfing and outdoor activities at the beach. I also heard the climbing club was a lot of fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Diving course, go surf, surf camp, spend days at the beach, go party with your friends, go on hikes around Sydney, go to the Blue Mountains, go see a concert in the Opera house, go to sport events, BBQ at the beach, 
Longer time off (spring break i.e.):  Travel the East coast (Cairns to Brisbane), Melbourne (and Great Ocean Road), Byron Bay,

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty easy, the lifestyle in Coogee (Sydney) fitted me very well. It's a beach suburb of Sydney and the vibe is very laid back, people are very active and friendly. 
I lived with many danes and dutch people so the culture wasn't that different in the house.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in class and get coffee together after class, help each other out. If it's somebody who's interesting, plan to do something after class. A good ice-breaker is also to ask for advice or good ideas of what to do in the area (food places, places to go out etc.).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any differences I found challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very friendly and easy to talk to. The laid back, sun-is-always-shining vibe also suited me very well. The opportunity to do activities in the everyday life that you don't normally do in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Choose classes so you are flexible to plan your week, be open and attend everything social etc in the beginning, don't hesitate to ask and reach out to other students/professors for help, advice or just to chat.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of things you can commit to (social wise) so it's just about choosing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the memories we created together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
To balance study and socializing/exploring.
Make sure to attend study but also prioritize social cultural experiences.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
